title: Intent data, honestly: what it tells you and what it doesn't
summary: A clear, honest guide to intent data: first-party vs third-party, account-level vs contact-level, where it misleads you, and how to use it well.
body_text: Intent data is supposed to tell you who's ready to buy. More often it tells you something much weaker: that someone at a company you care about looked at a topic you sell into, sometime in the last week or two. That's useful for prioritizing. It doesn't tell you a real buyer is in-market, and it definitely doesn't tell you which person to reach. Most teams buy the third-party, account-level version: a vendor infers that "Acme is surging on your category" from research happening on other people's websites. The signal that actually holds up is first-party and contact-level, what a named person did on your site and ads. Same words, very different signal. This piece walks through both and gets honest about where each one actually helps. What is intent data, exactly? Intent data is behavioral data used to infer that a person or company is researching a product or category, and might be moving toward a purchase. The key word is infer . You're not reading anyone's mind. You're watching digital behavior, page views, content downloads, search activity, review-site visits, ad clicks, and estimating interest from it. Two distinctions decide how much that estimate is worth: where the data comes from, and how precisely it identifies the person. First-party vs third-party intent data First-party intent data is behavior on your own properties: your site, your pricing page, your ads, your webinars. You control it, you can see it in near real time, and it points at people who already found you. Third-party (often sold as "purchase intent data") is aggregated from other websites, publisher networks, and review sites, then modeled into a topic score for an account. It gives you reach into companies that never touched your site, which is its whole appeal. As Foundry puts it in its breakdown of intent data types , third-party intent "reveals account interests and topics across the internet but it does not necessarily indicate buying intent." Hold onto that sentence. Account-level vs contact-level The second distinction is the one the category keeps skipping. Most B2B intent data is account-level: it resolves to a logo, not a human. "A company in your ICP is researching data security" is a very different asset than "the VP of Security at that company read your comparison page twice this week." Account-level intent tells you something is happening at the company. A named contact is someone your rep can call this afternoon. Before you trust any intent feed, know which two boxes it sits in: first-party or third-party, account-level or contact-level. That combination tells you more about the feed's value than any vendor pitch will. Where third-party intent data misleads you Third-party, account-level intent is the noisiest, latest signal in your stack, and it's usually the one sold hardest. This is where it burns teams. It's late. By the time a topic surge shows up in a modeled feed, the buyer may already have a shortlist. You're reacting to research that happened days or weeks ago, on someone else's timeline. It doesn't tell you who. "Acme is hot" is not a person. Acme might have two thousand employees. Your reps can't call a logo, and handing them a hot account with no name just moves the guesswork downstream. Your competitors bought the same list. Third-party intent is sold to anyone who pays for it , and only a slice of those signals map to accounts genuinely moving toward a purchase. If everyone selling into that account sees the same surge, it's not an edge. Interest is not intent. Someone constantly reading about a category can have deep curiosity and zero budget, like a person who browses luxury-car sites every night but drives a 10-year-old hatchback. Topic consumption is interest. Treating it as a purchase decision erodes sales' trust in the whole program fast. None of this means third-party intent is worthless. It means it's a prioritization layer. Use account-level intent to decide where to point attention, then corroborate with something closer to the buyer before you build a play around it. The signal that actually holds up The durable signal is first-party and contact-level: a named person from a company you care about, doing something meaningful on your own properties. A director at a target account who visited your pricing page, clicked an ad, and came back three days later is worth more than a whole account "surging" on a topic somewhere off in a data broker's model. You saw the behavior yourself. It's fresh, and you can tie it to a human. This is the layer Vector is built on. We de-anonymize the real contacts landing on your site and ads, filter them to your ICP, and let you act on the actual person. Be honest about the boundary, though. First-party behavior only covers people who actually reach you (roughly a third of US B2B site traffic resolves to a named contact), so it won't show you accounts that never visited. That's exactly why the two work together: third-party for reach and prioritization, first-party for the signal you build real plays on. For the mechanics of the people-level version, see contact-level targeting . Weight your scoring and your spend toward behavior you can see on your own properties and attach to a name. How to actually use intent data A signal sitting in a dashboard changes nothing. The teams that get value from intent data score it, prioritize with it, and get to the right person fast. The common failure is raw signals sprayed into a dozen Slack channels with no scoring and no play, so nobody works them and the program stalls. Score and prioritize Blend fit and behavior into one score. Fit is how closely the company and the person match your ICP. Behavior is what they actually did, and how recently. A pricing-page visit from an in-ICP director outranks a topic surge from an account nobody can name. Your ICP is a precision dial. Tighten it and volume drops but false positives fall too. Loosen it and you pay to reach non-buyers. Set that expectation before you cut the audience down. For a longer walkthrough of turning scores into moves, read what to do with intent data . Reach the right person with the right message, fast Once a signal fires, three things have to line up. Start with the person, the actual buyer or committee member at the account, which isn't always whoever happened to click the most. Then match the message to where that person sits in the buying group, because one ad aimed at everyone from the CIO to a project manager lands with nobody. Then get it to them on a channel that hits, usually contact-level paid on LinkedIn, Google, or Meta, sometimes a scoped alert that routes the named contact to the owning rep for a same-day touch. Speed matters here. Warm behavior goes cold quickly. For the activation side specifically, see how to act on buyer interest , and if you're building the business case, the ROI of ABM intent data lays out the math. Treat intent data as an input Intent data earns its place when you treat it honestly. Third-party, account-level intent points you at where to look. It won't tell you a deal is real or name a buyer, and your competitors are reading the same feeds. First-party, contact-level behavior is the signal you can actually build on, because you watched it happen and you can attach it to a person. Score both together, move fast to the right human, and weight your budget toward the signal you can verify. If you want to see what that looks like when identity resolution, scoring, and activation run in one system, that's what Vector is built for .

title: Oligometastatic Disease in Real-World Radiology: The ECR 2026 Award-Winning Study That Reveals a Critical Gap
summary: A large-scale analysis of 33.7 million radiology reports uncovers how rarely radiologists independently document oligometastatic disease and why that matters for patient outcomes.
body_text: A large-scale analysis of 33.7 million radiology reports uncovers how rarely radiologists independently document oligometastatic disease and why that matters for patient outcomes. At ECR 2026 , the European Congress of Radiology in Vienna, the world's second-largest radiology congress, one of Segmed’s studies stood out . Among 11,376 submitted abstracts, an observational study through real-world data analysis of oligometastatic disease (OMD) documentation in routine U.S. radiology practice was recognized with the Best Research Presentation Abstract Award, on the topic of Oncologic Imaging. For a field still debating whether AI or structured reporting will close the gap between imaging interpretation and clinical decision-making, this study reframes the question entirely. The gap is not technological: it is linguistic, habitual, and measurable. And it is happening right now, in routine practice, across millions of reports. This blog breaks down what the study found, why it matters, and what it signals for the future of structured reporting and AI-assisted oncologic imaging. ‍ ‍ The Researcher Team Behind the Award The ECR 2026 Best Research Presentation Abstract Award was received in Vienna by Martin Willemink, MD, PhD , our very own Co-founder & Chief Scientific Officer. Martin accepted the recognition at the Awards Ceremony in front of delegates from 121 countries. ‍ Dr. Martin Willemink received the Best Research Presentation Abstract Award at the ECR 2026 Awards Ceremony in Vienna, March 2026, from Prof. Matthias Prokop, Chair of the Radiology Department at Radboud University in Nijmegen, The Netherlands. ‍ The study was conducted by our multidisciplinary team across Segmed: Jie Wu, PhD (Co-founder and Chief of AI), Aline Lutz de Araujo, MD, PhD (Vice President of RWE and Clinical Insights), Martin Willemink and Sean Khozin, MD, MPH (Physician-scientist and CEO of the CEORT - CEO Roundtable on Cancer & Project Data Sphere) , combining expertise in data science, clinical research, and radiology to design and execute the analysis at a scale that would not have been possible without Segmed's real-world imaging data platform. The award, presented by the European Society of Radiology (ESR), recognizes the best-rated research presentation abstract per topic as selected by the ECR 2026 Scientific Subcommittees. Winners receive free registration to the subsequent congress alongside a certificate. But more importantly, recognition from one of the field's most respected bodies that the study is worth the community's attention. That this honor was given to a study grounded in real-world data (not a controlled trial, not a simulation) is itself a signal. It reflects a growing recognition within radiology that understanding current practice is just as important as designing ideal practice. ‍ What Is Oligometastatic Disease and Why Does Reporting It Matter? Oligometastatic disease (OMD) describes an intermediate state of cancer spread: more than localized disease, but less than widespread metastasis. Typically defined as 1-5 metastatic lesions, OMD represents a clinically meaningful threshold because patients in this state may still be candidates for aggressive, curative-intent local therapies, including Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT), surgical metastatectomy, and thermal ablation. The decision to pursue these interventions almost always begins with an imaging report. The radiologist's documentation of lesion count, location, disease trajectory, and prior treatment history directly shapes the multidisciplinary discussion that follows. When that documentation is consistent and precise, it opens doors for patients who might benefit from targeted treatment. When it is absent or imprecise, those opportunities may go unrecognized. ‍ The clinical spectrum from localized to polymetastatic disease with oligometastatic disease as the critical intermediate where curative-intent local therapy may still be possible. (From the ECR 2026 presentation by Wu, Lutz de Araujo, Khozin & Willemink) ‍ Radiology that consistently recognizes and communicates OMD - relevant features creates the conditions for optimal treatment selection. Radiology that does not may inadvertently close doors for patients who could benefit from curative-intent local therapy. ‍ The Study: What Did 33.7 Million Reports Reveal? ‍ The award-winning research conducted a large-scale retrospective analysis of real-world radiology reports drawn from across the United States, 33.7 million reports spanning 40 states. Researchers searched for mentions of oligometastatic disease using terminology consistent with the ESTRO-EORTC classification framework. The results were revealing: Out of the tens of millions of exams, only 164 reports were found that mentioned oligometastatic disease (OMD) or a variant (e.g. oligometastasis). Of the 164 reports that mentioned OMD, clinicians referring physicians, oncologists, and other non-radiology team members provided the OMD context in the indication or clinical history field in 148 reports from 95 patients. Radiologists independently used the term OMD in their own report narrative in just 18 reports from 17 patients. That is the central finding of the study recognized with the Best Research Presentation Abstract Award at ECR 2026: a large-scale, real-world observational analysis of how oligometastatic disease (OMD) is used or more accurately, how rarely it is used in routine radiology practice across the United States. ‍ OMD mentions in radiology reports by year (2017–2025). The first recorded mention appeared in 2017, years after the clinical concept was established, and total adoption has remained minimal across 33.7 million reports. (From the ECR 2026 presentation by Wu, Lutz de Araujo, Khozin & Willemink) ‍ Why Radiology Reports Are the Front Line for OMD When a patient presents with limited metastatic disease, the decision of whether they might benefit from aggressive local treatment Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT), surgical metastatectomy, or thermal ablation typically begins with an imaging report. How that report frames lesion count, location, prior treatment history, and disease trajectory shapes the multidisciplinary discussion that follows. Radiology that consistently recognizes and communicates OMD-relevant features creates the conditions for optimal treatment selection. Radiology that does not may inadvertently close doors for patients who could benefit from curative-intent local therapy. ‍ Why Real-World Data Is the Right Tool for This Question Clinical trials, by design, select for ideal conditions. Patients are screened, definitions are standardized, and the clinical team is attuned to the specific criteria under study. Real-world data cuts through that filter. It reveals what happens when a concept moves from the protocol to the routine clinical practice. For OMD, a real-world analysis of routine radiology practice offers something clinical trials cannot: an honest baseline . It revealed how often radiologists are using OMD-consistent language, which aspects of the ESTRO-EORTC classification framework are making it into reports, whether patterns differ by tumor type or imaging modality, and where education or structured reporting tools might produce the greatest gains. This kind of work was singled out for recognition at ECR 2026 speaks to a broader disciplinary maturation. The field is not merely asking can radiology contribute to OMD management. It is beginning to ask, rigorously and empirically, how well is it currently doing so? ‍ Recognition at the world's second-largest radiology congress sends a clear signal: translational, practice-anchored research is not a lesser endeavour: it is an urgent one. ‍ The Role of Real-World Data Infrastructure ‍ Studies like this one are not possible without the right data infrastructure. Analyzing 33.7 million radiology reports requires not only scale, but also the ability to search, filter, and surface signal across highly heterogeneous clinical documentation: different EHR systems, report formats, terminology conventions, and institutional practices. This is precisely where platforms purpose-built for real-world medical data, like Segmed, become essential. Access to large, de-identified, multi-institutional datasets, along with the tools to query them effectively, is what transforms a clinically interesting hypothesis into a publishable, award-winning finding. For research teams exploring questions in oncologic imaging, structured reporting, AI model development, or clinical decision support, the availability of this kind of data is not a background condition. It is the research. ‍ What Comes Next: Structured Reporting and AI-Assisted OMD Identification The findings from this study point directly toward two areas of opportunity for the radiology community: ‍ 1. Structured Reporting Templates If radiologists are not independently documenting OMD-relevant features, one path forward is to make it easier for them to do so, through structured reporting templates that prompt for lesion count, prior treatment history, and disease trajectory in relevant oncologic contexts. The evidence base for designing these templates well now exists. 2. AI-Assisted Lesion Characterization AI tools that automatically flag OMD-consistent findings, based on lesion number, location, and progression patterns, could provide real-time decision support at the point of interpretation. These tools, however, need to be grounded in what radiologists actually document, not what a trial protocol assumes they do. Studies like the one recognized at ECR 2026 provide exactly that foundation. A Signal Worth Paying Attention To The gap between how OMD is defined in clinical literature and how it appears, or doesn't, in routine radiology reports is not a minor documentation issue. It is a clinical gap with real consequences for patients who might otherwise be considered for curative-intent therapy. The study recognized at ECR 2026 names that gap precisely, at scale, with real-world evidence. title: Tips to Quit Drinking
summary: Here at Reframe, we want to meet you on your journey, wherever you're at. This article will detail a couple important tips to quit drinking, and if you're interested on taking some steps toward cutting back or stopping alcohol use with us, download the Reframe app. We'd love to have you.
body_text: If you've landed on this page, you're probably in a place where you're considering taking a break from alcohol or cutting it out of your life completely. Here at Reframe, we want to meet you on your journey, wherever you're at. This article will detail a couple important tips to quit drinking, and if you're interested on taking some steps toward cutting back or stopping alcohol use with us, download the Reframe app. We'd love to have you. Determine your "why." This is made up of some of the reasons you're considering quitting or cutting back on drinking. These reasons could be physical, emotional, or have to do with relationships. When you can identify your "why," you can always come back to it when you need to center yourself. Find a support system/community. One of the best things you can do is to surround yourself with people who support you. Identify trusted members of your network and confide in them. You can also find communities online or in-person with others who are on a similar journey. This way, you can hold each other accountable and be there for one another throughout this process. Practice turning down a drink. In our culture, drinking alcohol is extremely commonplace, and it may even go against the current to turn down a drink. Take time to practice ways to say "no." Change your environment. Remove alcohol from your home. Take a different route to work that doesn't pass by the liquor store. In changing simple environmental factors, you can remove yourself from situations that may lead you to drink. Self-care & coping mechanisms. Oftentimes, we drink alcohol as a form of coping. Replace the time you'd spend drinking with other self-care and coping mechanisms, such as exercise, a new hobby, journaling, etc. Learn the benefits. If you haven't read our article about the benefits of cutting down on drinking yet, check it out here. When you know of the benefits you're gaining from a changed relationship with alcohol, it may encourage you to keep going. Have grit and persistence despite setbacks. It's incredibly common to experience setbacks, and it doesn't make you any less. When you experience a setback, reach out to your support system. Remind yourself that you can do this, and you can keep going. Your progress is not defined by a bump in the road. Remember, you've got this. We at Reframe are here to support and help you along this journey. Join us today, and begin working toward a more fulfilling life. ‍ ‍

title: How to Send Money from Nigeria to Belgium
summary: How to send money from Nigeria to Belgium. Compare Wise, Remitly, Afriex, and bank wires. Tips on fees, NGN/EUR rates, and CBN documentation.
body_text: Belgium rarely comes up in conversations about the Nigerian diaspora. The UK, Italy, Canada: those dominate the conversation. But Belgium has a quiet and substantial Nigerian presence, and for the tens of thousands of Nigerians between Brussels and Antwerp, the question of how to send money back and forth is one that comes up constantly, and the answers are worse than they should be. I have been watching this corridor closely. It hits almost every pain point that makes African diaspora transfers difficult: currency controls on the Nigerian side, EU AML compliance on the Belgian side, and a market that the big international remittance brands have never fully optimized for. The result is that most Nigerians in Belgium are either overpaying through their bank or relying on services built for a different audience. This post is my attempt to give you a proper walkthrough. Why Nigerians in Belgium Are a Bigger Community Than You Think The Belgian context matters. Brussels is home to the EU institutions (the European Commission, the European Parliament, the Council of the EU) and attracts African professionals working in diplomacy, NGOs, international development, and policy. Antwerp is one of the world's major diamond trade hubs, and West African traders have been part of that ecosystem for decades. Add the university students at KU Leuven, Vrije Universiteit Brussel, and Universiteit Antwerpen, and you have a Nigerian community that is educated, economically active, and regularly sending money between Nigeria and Belgium in both directions. My estimate, based on migration data, is that at least 20,000 Nigerians live in Belgium at any given time, likely more when you account for students on temporary visas and undocumented residents. That is a meaningful corridor, and it is systematically underserved by the mainstream transfer industry. The Structural Problems With This Corridor On the surface, Nigeria to Belgium should be easy. Both countries have functional banking systems and both are connected to SWIFT. Belgium uses the euro, which is among the most liquid currencies in the world. The friction is not technical. It is regulatory and structural on both sides. From the Nigerian side, the Central Bank of Nigeria has placed significant restrictions on outbound foreign exchange over the last several years. Sending money internationally from a Nigerian bank account requires proper documentation of purpose (education, medical, family support, business), and some banks are more cooperative than others in processing these requests. The permitted annual forex allocation for individuals has changed multiple times, and the rules are not uniformly applied across banks. What this means in practice is that a straightforward transfer request can stall for days at a local bank branch while the officer figures out what approval is required. From the Belgian side, the country operates under strict EU Anti-Money Laundering regulations, and Belgium's financial intelligence unit (CTIF-CFI) pays close attention to incoming transfers from West Africa. Transfers above certain thresholds get additional scrutiny. This is not a barrier to legitimate transfers, but it means using a properly regulated service matters here more than it might in other corridors. What the Nigerian Community in Belgium Actually Uses When I look at how people actually navigate this corridor, the pattern falls into roughly three groups. The first group relies on Western Union and MoneyGram, particularly for sending money from Belgium to Nigeria. The reason is familiarity. The recipients in Nigeria know how to pick up Western Union, and it works without requiring a bank account. The cost, though, is real. On a 300 euro transfer, you can easily lose 20 to 30 euros in fees and exchange rate spread. Over twelve months, that number accumulates into something significant. The second group uses their Belgian bank to send directly. ING Belgium, KBC, BNP Paribas Fortis, and Belfius all process SWIFT international transfers, and a Nigerian bank account receiving a SWIFT wire is standard procedure. The problem is cost at both ends. The sending Belgian bank charges outbound transfer fees of 20 to 35 euros per transaction depending on the amount and speed. The receiving Nigerian bank often charges its own fee on inbound international transfers. And neither of those fees includes the exchange rate margin that the bank takes as profit, which is typically 1.5 to 3 percent above the mid-market rate. The third group, and these are the people who have figured it out, uses digital transfer platforms that specialize in corridors like Nigeria-Belgium. Wise, Remitly, and Afriex all serve this route and offer materially better outcomes than a bank wire. The Real Comparison: What Each Option Costs You Let me be concrete, because vague descriptions of "lower fees" are not useful when you are trying to decide where to send 500 euros. Bank wire transfers are the most expensive option for most transfer sizes. For amounts below 2,000 euros, the flat fee plus rate margin almost always makes this the worst choice. Where bank wires make sense is for very large amounts, above 5,000 euros, where the percentage-based fee structures of digital platforms start to approach what a bank charges in flat fees. Western Union and MoneyGram retain a use case specifically when cash pickup at a Nigerian agent location is the delivery method. If your recipient does not have a bank account, these services are reliable. If they do have a bank account, you are paying a premium for a delivery method you do not need. Wise is one of the most transparent options in this corridor. The platform shows you the mid-market EUR/NGN rate, tells you the fee upfront, and shows the exact naira amount the recipient will receive before you confirm. The limitation is that delivery is bank account to bank account, and in my experience the processing time for first-time transfers is occasionally longer than advertised while identity verification completes. Remitly covers this corridor with competitive pricing and a mobile-first experience that works well for regular transfers. Speed and rate offers vary by time of day, so checking mid-week during business hours often yields the best available rates. Afriex was built specifically with the African diaspora in mind, and the Nigeria-Belgium corridor is one we have worked to make competitive. My honest recommendation, as always, is to compare. Pull up the EUR/NGN rate on XE.com or Wise, then check what Afriex and Remitly are each offering for the same amount on the same day. The received naira amount is the number that tells you everything. I'd encourage you to run that comparison across at least two services before committing to a routine. What to Have Ready Before You Transfer This is the part that trips people up, and delays happen because of missing information rather than anything wrong with the transfer itself. To send money to a Nigerian bank account from Belgium, you need: the recipient's full legal name exactly as registered on their bank account, the 10-digit NUBAN account number, the bank name, and the bank's SWIFT/BIC code. The name match matters enormously for Nigerian bank transfers. A nickname, a shortened version of a middle name, or an initial where a full name is expected can cause the bank to hold or return the transfer. Check the recipient's bank card or account statement and copy the name exactly. For transfers above 1,000 euros, Belgian banks and regulated transfer services operating under EU rules may ask you to state the purpose. "Family support" is a recognized and accepted category. "Education fees" works for student support. Have a brief description ready. It keeps the process moving without additional back-and-forth. For transfers originating in Nigeria to Belgium, the primary challenge is the forex access. The most reliable approach is to use a licensed International Money Transfer Operator (IMTO) that is registered with the CBN and operates within the approved framework. These services can access foreign exchange and process the transfer through legitimate channels. Trying to do this through an informal arrangement because it seems faster or cheaper is a risk that is genuinely not worth taking. The exposure to loss is real, and there is no recourse. Tracking the EUR/NGN Exchange Rate The exchange rate between the euro and the naira is where real money disappears without people realizing it, and it has been more volatile over the last three years than most Nigerians sending regular support had planned for. My habit, and one I share with anyone who transfers money regularly, is to check the mid-market EUR/NGN rate on XE.com before initiating any transfer. The mid-market rate is the baseline. It is what the currency markets are actually trading at. Every transfer service applies a margin to that rate as their profit. Knowing the baseline tells you whether a particular service's offer on a given day is reasonable or expensive. The practical implication for people sending regular support from Belgium to Nigeria: if you have a naira amount in mind as the monthly support target, work backward from the EUR/NGN rate to figure out how many euros to send. Do not work forward from a fixed euro amount, because the naira amount arriving will vary with the rate. A 200 euro transfer that delivered 320,000 naira six months ago might deliver 290,000 naira today if the rate has moved. For Business Transfers The Nigeria-Belgium corridor also includes a meaningful volume of business payments: small importers in Lagos paying Belgian companies for goods, Nigerian consultants billing EU-based clients, professionals receiving salary payments from Belgian employers into Nigerian accounts. For business transfers, the compliance requirements are higher and worth understanding in advance. Belgian companies sending payment to Nigeria will typically require a formal invoice and may need to classify the payment in their accounting. Nigerian businesses receiving payments from Belgium should work with a bank or transfer service that can issue a proper inbound remittance certificate, which is useful for Nigerian tax documentation. The size of the transfer matters here. For amounts above 10,000 euros, both Belgian and Nigerian financial institutions have additional reporting requirements. These are manageable with proper documentation. They are not barriers to the transfer. But walking into the process unprepared adds unnecessary time. Closing The Nigeria-Belgium corridor is one of those routes that works well when you understand it, and causes unnecessary friction and expense when you do not. The community of Nigerians in Belgium is real, active, and regularly moving money across this corridor. The tools to do it cheaply and efficiently exist today. The thing I see most often is people using their bank out of habit because that is what they have always done. Compare that bank rate against what a digital platform offers for the same transfer. Do it once. The number you see will likely be enough to change your routine.

title: How AI Pipeline Insights Help You Prepare for Better Pipeline Review Meetings

body_text: Pipeline review meetings are some of the most important conversations sales managers have each week. They're where you identify deal risk, coach reps through opportunities, and make sure your forecast reflects reality. But preparing for those meetings can be time-consuming. If you've ever bounced between Salesforce reports, spreadsheets, dashboards, and CRM notes trying to understand what changed since your last review, you're not alone. One question our Support team hears often is: Can Ambition help me prepare for pipeline review meetings? The answer is yes. Ambition's AI Pipeline Insights summarize your team's pipeline activity, highlight meaningful changes, and give you the context you need before the meeting starts so you can spend less time gathering information and more time coaching. Why Pipeline Review Preparation Takes So Long Most sales managers don't struggle with running pipeline reviews. They struggle with preparing for them. Before the meeting, you may need to answer questions like: Which opportunities were added this week? Which deals slipped? Where did pipeline value increase or decrease? Which reps need coaching? How has pipeline coverage changed? Are there any deals that deserve extra attention? Finding those answers usually means reviewing multiple reports and manually connecting the dots. That preparation can easily take longer than the meeting itself. How Ambition's AI Pipeline Insights Help Ambition uses AI to analyze pipeline activity and generate summaries that help managers quickly understand what's happening across their team. Instead of manually reviewing dozens of opportunities, you receive a clear overview of the changes that matter most. Depending on what you're reviewing, you can generate insights for: An individual sales rep Your entire team A manager's organization Larger revenue organizations This flexibility makes it easy to prepare for weekly coaching conversations, leadership reviews, or executive forecast meetings. What Information Is Included? Pipeline Insights combine AI-generated summaries with visual reporting so managers can understand both the details and the bigger picture. Each summary can include: Recent Pipeline Changes Quickly see which opportunities were: Added Removed Updated Advanced Delayed Instead of hunting through reports, you immediately understand what changed since your last review. AI Summary of Pipeline Activity Ambition generates a written summary that highlights meaningful trends and notable pipeline movement. Rather than reading dozens of opportunity updates, you get an easy-to-digest overview that helps you prepare talking points before the meeting. Pipeline Stage Breakdown Visual charts show where deals currently sit throughout the pipeline. This makes it easier to identify bottlenecks, stalled opportunities, or areas where coaching may be needed. Pipeline Value Flow See how total pipeline value has changed over your selected time period so you can quickly evaluate overall pipeline health. Customize the Time Period That Matters Every pipeline review has a different purpose. Sometimes you're reviewing this week's changes. Other times you're preparing for a monthly business review or quarterly forecast. Pipeline Insights let you adjust your reporting window so you can analyze activity across the timeframe that's most relevant to your conversation. Save Your Favorite Pipeline Views If you regularly prepare the same reports, you don't have to rebuild them every time. You can save custom Pipeline Views for future use and quickly return to the reports your team relies on most. This is especially helpful for managers who run recurring pipeline reviews with the same format each week. Share Pipeline Views Across Your Team Need everyone reviewing the same data? You can share Pipeline View templates with other managers or stakeholders to ensure everyone is working from a consistent view of the pipeline. Standardized reporting creates more productive conversations because everyone starts with the same information. Schedule Reports Automatically If your leadership team expects regular pipeline updates, Ambition can help there too. Scheduled Pipeline Intelligence Reports can be automatically emailed to you or other stakeholders on a recurring basis. Instead of remembering to run reports every Monday morning, the insights arrive automatically. How Sales Managers Use Pipeline Insights Many managers use Pipeline Insights as part of their regular coaching workflow. A typical process looks like this: Generate Pipeline Insights before the meeting. Review the AI summary and pipeline changes. Identify deals that need discussion. Use the visual pipeline breakdown to spot trends. Walk into the meeting with clear coaching priorities instead of spending time gathering updates. The result is a more focused conversation centered on strategy, deal progression, and coaching instead of searching for information. Frequently Asked Questions Can Ambition summarize my team's pipeline with AI? Yes. Pipeline Insights generate AI-powered summaries for individual reps, teams, or larger organizations, helping managers quickly understand pipeline activity before review meetings. Can I customize what timeframe I'm reviewing? Yes. You can generate Pipeline Insights for different reporting periods, including weekly, monthly, or quarterly reviews. Can I save Pipeline Views? Absolutely. Pipeline Views can be saved for future use, making recurring pipeline reviews much faster to prepare. Can I share Pipeline Views with other managers? Yes. Saved Pipeline View templates can be shared across your organization so everyone reviews consistent pipeline data. Can Pipeline reports be emailed automatically? Yes. Scheduled Pipeline Intelligence Reports can be delivered automatically to you or other stakeholders. Preparing for Pipeline Reviews Shouldn't Be the Hardest Part Pipeline review meetings are most valuable when managers spend their time discussing strategy, coaching reps, and making decisions, not searching through reports. Ambition's AI Pipeline Insights help simplify preparation by bringing together pipeline summaries, visual reporting, opportunity changes, and scheduled reporting in one place. That means you can walk into every pipeline review with the context you need to have a more productive conversation. If you're looking to save time while making your pipeline reviews more focused and actionable, Pipeline Insights are a great place to start. title: Best Wireless Security System Cameras for Small Businesses
summary: Highly-rated, reliable wireless security system cameras for small shops and retail locations. Find out more inside.
body_text: Video quality: If you can’t see what’s going on in your wireless security system camera feed, you won’t be able to use that data to make your business safer. A wireless camera that records at least 2K video will strike a great balance between visibility and file size, allowing you to capture finer details. If you need an even bigger boost in video quality, consider picking up a 4K wireless security camera. Battery life: Since you’re running your security network without wires, you need a way to power your cameras for day-in, day-out recording. Long-lasting rechargeable batteries will power your cameras for months, and ensuring that they’re swappable means you can keep them going with minimal downtime. Motion detection: Recording your business after-hours helps boost overall security, but constant 24/7 coverage can drain your batteries. Built-in motion detection features can help you record the most important moments without wearing down battery life or filling up your data storage. Ease of use: You’re already busy enough running your business. The last thing you need to worry about is how to view and operate your security feed. The best wireless security cameras for business include intuitive and user-friendly apps so you can manage your camera network from a desktop or mobile device.
